To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) left posterior temporal regions, (ii) supramarginal cortex and (iii) Broca's area are involved in verbal shortterm memory.
the brain areas underlying the processes involved in VSTM are located in left posterior temporal cortex, left supramargimal gyrus and left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex.

(a) the left posterior temporal lobe is involved in the recoding of visual into phonological codes; (b) the left supramargimal gyrus is involved in the storage of phonological codes; and (c) the left dorsolateral pre-motor cortex is involved with the temporal grouping of phonological codes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cognitive processes involved in VSTM, and the neuroanatomical basis of these processes.
the neural basis of VSTM and the cognitive processes that underlie it.
the neural basis of verbal working memory, a topic that has been the focus of considerable recent interest.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the left-lateralised network of areas revealed in this study is involved in the phonological maintenance of verbal sequences, with a possible role for the premotor cortex in the rhythmic control of rehearsal.
the neural basis of the storage and rehearsal processes in VSTM is still not well understood.

the left-lateralised VSTM network is involved in the representation and rehearsal of verbal items and their temporal organisation, and that this network can be divided into functionally specialised areas that subserve these processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
recoding is a left posterior temporal process, storage and rehearsal are left supramargimal processes and grouping is a left dorsolateral pre-motor process.

VSTM for sequences of visual items involves left posterior temporal areas for the recoding of visual items into phonological representations, left supramarginals for storage of these phonological representations and left dorsolateral pre-motor cortex for the rhythmic organisation and rehearsal of the stored information.
the brain areas involved in VSTM can be identified in terms of a functional network that includes posterior and inferior temporal cortex, supramarginals, Broca's and dorsolateral frontal areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain areas involved in the processing of VSTM are not as localised as previously thought.
the brain areas involved in VSTM are not limited to those associated with storage, but include areas that support the processes of recoding, rehearsal and temporal grouping.

the functional neuroanatomy of verbal working memory has been mapped with a high degree of specificity, which should allow the study of its dysfunction in patients and the development of more effective treatments.
